title: 1956 AHSME Problem 27
statement: If an angle of a triangle remains unchanged but each of its two including sides is doubled, then the area is multiplied by:

solutions.text:
If the included sides are \(a\) and \(b,\) and their unchanged angle is \(C,\) the original area is \(\frac12ab\sin C.\) After both sides are doubled, the area is \[ \begin{gathered} \frac12(2a)(2b)\sin C \\ =2ab\sin C\\ =4\left(\frac12ab\sin C\right). \end{gathered} \]

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: Use the area formula \(\frac12ab\sin C\) for two sides and their included angle
Doubling both side factors multiplies their product by \(2\cdot2\)
